items.statement:
Let $S^2:=\{n\in\mathbb R^3:n\cdot n=1\}$ with the smooth structure given by the six graph charts solving $n_j=\pm\sqrt{1-\sum_{k\ne j}n_k^2}$ on the hemispheres $\pm n_j>0$. Orient it outward using the ordered spatial basis $x^1,x^2,x^3$. Its tangent plane is $T_nS^2=\{X\in\mathbb R^3:n\cdot X=0\}$. Physically, $n=k/|k|$ for a nonzero spatial wavevector $k$ in the SI Fourier description, where $k$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$; hence $n$ is dimensionless and the radial magnitude is discarded. For $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$, set $C_nz:=i\,n\times z$, $P_T(n)z:=z-n(n\cdot z)$, and $P_\sigma(n):=\tfrac12(P_T(n)+\sigma C_n)$ on $\mathbb C^3$, using the complex-linear extension of the right-handed cross product. Define the helicity fibre $L_\sigma(n):=\operatorname{range}P_\sigma(n)$ and the total space $L_\sigma:=\{(n,z):n\in S^2,\ z\in L_\sigma(n)\}$, projected to $S^2$ by $(n,z)\mapsto n$. Use the Hermitian product $\langle u,v\rangle_H:=\sum_{j=1}^3\overline{u_j}v_j$.

On a spherical chart with $0<\theta<\pi$ and a smooth longitude branch $\phi$, write $n=(\sin\theta\cos\phi,\sin\theta\sin\phi,\cos\theta)$, $e_\theta=(\cos\theta\cos\phi,\cos\theta\sin\phi,-\sin\theta)$, and $e_\phi=(-\sin\phi,\cos\phi,0)$. The local unit helicity frame is $v_\sigma:=(e_\theta+i\sigma e_\phi)/\sqrt2$. For any local smooth unit frame $v$ of $L_\sigma$, define its Berry connection one-form by $A:=i v^\dagger d v$, where $d v$ differentiates its three complex components. A smooth phase change $v'=e^{i\chi}v$, with real smooth $\chi$, changes this local form to $A'=A-d\chi$. The local Berry curvature is the two-form $F:=dA$; this definition makes no global gluing assertion.
items.physical_scope: Conditional classical Maxwell-Lorentz vacuum model in the smooth source-free nonzero-Fourier-mode regime stated by the supplier. The construction is the direction-sphere geometry of those modes, with no additional approximation. Directions, unit polarization vectors, the helicity sigma, and angular coordinates are dimensionless; the Berry connection and holonomy are dimensionless. There is no quantization, photon position operator, material medium, measurement, or empirical claim.

items.title: Curvature and the obstruction to a global polarization basis

references.title: K. Y. Bliokh, F. J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, F. Nori and A. V. Zayats, Spin-orbit interactions of light, Nature Photonics 9 (2015), arXiv:1505.02864

references.title: David Tong, The Quantum Hall Effect, TIFR Infosys Lecture Notes (2016)
references.locator: §1.5.1–1.5.2, printed pp. 28–34: gauge changes, curvature, surface phase, and the spin-in-a-field monopole calculation. Tong uses the opposite connection sign and a spin-1/2 quantum model; neither is imported as a premise.

items.statement: Fix $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$ and let $L_\sigma(n)$ be the range of the helicity projector $P_\sigma(n)$ over the outward-oriented unit sphere $S^2$. On an angular chart with $0<\theta<\pi$ and a smooth longitude branch $\phi$, use $v_\sigma=(e_\theta+i\sigma e_\phi)/\sqrt2$ and the connection convention $A_\sigma=i v_\sigma^\dagger d v_\sigma$. The spherical frame has Berry one-form $A_\sigma=\sigma\cos\theta\,d\phi$ and curvature $F_\sigma=dA_\sigma=-\sigma\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi$. If $\omega_{S^2,n}(X,Y):=n\cdot(X\times Y)$ is the outward area form for $X,Y\in T_nS^2$, then this curvature extends smoothly to the whole sphere as $F_\sigma=-\sigma\omega_{S^2}$. Write $\int_{S^2}$ for the outward-oriented integral, evaluated as the sum over the eight radially projected octant triangles described in the Proof. Its total flux is $\int_{S^2}F_\sigma=-4\pi\sigma$, so the flux divided by $2\pi$ is $-2\sigma$ in this convention. The line bundle has no globally smooth unit frame.
items.physical_scope: Conditional classical Maxwell-Lorentz vacuum model in the smooth source-free nonzero-Fourier-mode regime stated by the supplier, with no extra approximation. The result concerns the helicity line over nonzero wavevector directions, not a photon position operator, quantization, a material medium, an experiment, or an empirical claim.

items.title: SO(2) helicity character and geometric phase

references.title: K. Y. Bliokh, F. J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, F. Nori and A. V. Zayats, Spin-orbit interactions of light, Nature Photonics 9 (2015), arXiv:1505.02864
references.locator: Section 'Angular momenta and geometric phases', Box 2, PDF pp. 3–4: helicity phase under rotation and direction-sphere geometric phase; the active-rotation sign is derived here from the stated frame.

references.title: David Tong, The Quantum Hall Effect, TIFR Infosys Lecture Notes (2016)
references.locator: §1.5.1, printed pp. 28–31: parallel transport, local Berry connection, gauge transformation and surface-curvature phase. The classical connection convention here is recalculated explicitly.

items.statement: Fix $n\in S^2$ and $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$. Put $U(1):=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$. For the dimensionless angle $\alpha\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, define the proper active rotation fixing $n$ by $R_{n,\alpha}z=(n\cdot z)n+\cos\alpha\,(z-(n\cdot z)n)+\sin\alpha\,(n\times z)$ on $\mathbb C^3$, and set $SO(2)_n:=\{R_{n,\alpha}:\alpha\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)\}$. It acts on the whole helicity fibre $L_\sigma(n)$ by $R_{n,\alpha}z=e^{-i\sigma\alpha}z$, so the fibre carries the character $\rho_\sigma(R_{n,\alpha})=e^{-i\sigma\alpha}$. For a piecewise $C^1$ closed direction path $\gamma:[0,1]\to S^2$ with a finite subdivision $0=t_0<\cdots<t_m=1$ and local unit frames $v_j$ on the subpaths, define parallel transport by $\nabla s=P_\sigma ds=0$. If $v_{j+1}(\gamma(t_j))=g_jv_j(\gamma(t_j))$ at each internal join and $v_m(\gamma(1))=g_mv_1(\gamma(0))$, where $g_j,g_m\in U(1)$, then its holonomy, the scalar multiplying an initial fibre vector after transport around $\gamma$, is $\mathrm{Hol}_\gamma=\bigl(\prod_{j=1}^m\exp(i\int_{\gamma|[t_{j-1},t_j]}A_j)\bigr)\bigl(\prod_{j=1}^{m-1}g_j^{-1}\bigr)g_m$. In a single periodic frame this reduces to $\exp(i\oint_\gamma A)$. If a finite oriented smooth singular $2$-chain $\Sigma$ lies in one frame patch and $\partial\Sigma=\gamma$, then $\mathrm{Hol}_\gamma=\exp(i\int_\Sigma F_\sigma)$.
items.physical_scope: Conditional classical Maxwell-Lorentz vacuum model in the smooth source-free nonzero-Fourier-mode regime stated by the supplier, with no extra approximation. Rotations are proper active spatial rotations and parallel transport is that of the direction-sphere connection. This is the SO(2) helicity character, not a spin/orbital angular-momentum decomposition or a photon position operator; no dynamical time evolution, measured phase, material medium, quantization, or empirical claim is asserted.

items.title: Latitude-loop Berry holonomy

references.title: K. Y. Bliokh, F. J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, F. Nori and A. V. Zayats, Spin-orbit interactions of light, Nature Photonics 9 (2015), arXiv:1505.02864

references.title: David Tong, The Quantum Hall Effect, TIFR Infosys Lecture Notes (2016)
references.locator: §1.5.1–1.5.2, printed pp. 28–34: Berry phase as a connection integral and the surface solid-angle calculation. The spin-1/2 quantum model and its sign convention are not imported.

items.statement: Fix $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$ and $0<\theta_0<\pi$. Let $\gamma(t)=(\theta_0,2\pi t)$ for $0\le t\le1$ be the latitude loop in the direction sphere, and set $\Omega:=\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{\theta_0}\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\phi=2\pi(1-\cos\theta_0)$, the outward solid angle of its north cap. The spherical gauge gives $\mathrm{Hol}_\gamma=\exp(i2\pi\sigma\cos\theta_0)$. The north-pole regular gauge $v_N=e^{i\sigma\phi}v_\sigma$ has $A_N=\sigma(\cos\theta-1)d\phi$ and is smooth on the cap; its loop integral and the cap flux are both $-\sigma\Omega$. Hence $\mathrm{Hol}_\gamma=\exp(-i\sigma\Omega)=\exp(i2\pi\sigma\cos\theta_0)$.
items.physical_scope: A constructed path in the conditional classical Maxwell-Lorentz vacuum helicity model's smooth source-free nonzero-Fourier-mode regime, with no extra approximation. The loop, solid angle, and phase are dimensionless geometric quantities; no experimental measurement, material medium, quantization, or photon position operator is asserted.
